papers.title_en: GlassGround: GUI Grounding Beyond Native Screenshots with Egocentric Wearable Vision
papers.authors: Yun Wang, Siyue Sun, Jiaying Du, Xinyi Wei, Xiaoming Zhai, Zhenlin An, Ninghao Liu
papers.evidence: 将截图与可穿戴相机视角配对的 GUI 定位基准
papers.tldr: 可穿戴助手在无法获取截图时需从摄像头画面定位界面元素，但现有GUI定位基准主要基于原生截图。GlassGround将同一GUI状态下的原生截图与可穿戴相机视图配对，覆盖Android/iOS、4种设备和4种观看条件，共3250个任务。十个开源模型平均准确率从94.8%降至48.5%；PairDistill通过对齐跨视图目标表示并加入坐标监督，在无截图推理下提升9.4和12.2个百分点，结合局部缩放达69.6%和64.4%。该工作揭示了相机视图下的显著性能鸿沟，并提供基准与基线。
papers.abstract_en: Wearable assistants must localize interface elements from camera observations when direct screenshot access is unavailable, yet existing GUI grounding benchmarks primarily evaluate native screenshots. We introduce GlassGround, a new benchmark that pairs native screenshots with wearable camera observations while holding GUI states, instructions, and targets fixed. GlassGround contains 3,250 tasks across Android and iOS, captured using four wearable devices under four viewing conditions. Across ten open-source models, mean grounding accuracy drops from 94.8% on screenshots to 48.5% on camera images. Further analysis reveals that changes in target scale, screen geometry, and background cannot fully explain this performance degradation. We then study two ways to narrow this gap. At inference time, local zooming and screen rectification help but leave most of the gap. For training-time adaptation, we build on GlassGround's paired-view design and introduce PairDistill, a baseline that aligns target representations across views alongside coordinate supervision. Trained on independently collected data and using no screenshots at inference, it improves camera-image accuracy by 9.4 and 12.2 points on two backbones and transfers to unseen devices and operating systems. Combined with local zooming, it reaches 69.6% and 64.4%, but does not close the gap. The GlassGround dataset and code are available at https://github.com/yunnw/GlassGround.

papers.title_en: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
papers.authors: Hui Shen, Yunta Hsieh, Jianing Ma, Zhuoran Yin, Zhuhan Bao, Ziyuan Liu, Qi Han, Xiuqi Xu, Xianbang Wang, Wenhao Chai, Sihan Xu, Chenyang Zhao, Yanheng Shang, Dongfu Jiang, Rui Sun, Xingzhi Li, Chenqi Yin, Zesen Zhao, Boyuan Zheng, Jisen Li, Xiaoxia Wu, Ruoyan Zhang, Ruiyao Liu, Jing Xiong, He Xiao, Nan Zheng, Hangxiang Chen, Shengyang Tao, Deyang Luorong, Yifeng Liu, Jingxuan Zhang, Chaofan Tao, Yuren Wang, Jiaqi Mo, Rui Hu, Xing Wei, Xiaofeng Liu, Xin Xu, Han Wu, Mengyao Wen, Guobin Zhang, Shatong Zhu, Hei Ting Una Chan, Sicheng Chen, Kai Zhang, Mengkang Hu, Zhongwei Wan, Xin Wang, Chuanyang Zheng, Ziheng Zhang, Hengyuan Zhang, Zunhai Su, Kanzhi Cheng, Dehan Kong, Yian Wang, Hanrong Zhang, Jiawei Lu, Yifan Zhang, Junnan Li, Changyi Yang, Jintao Qu, Wenyao Gao, Jiaxuan Luo, Jiaxin Deng, Yuhao Chen, Xuesong Ye, Jingwen Gu, Yichi Zhang, Qun Lou, Shen Yan, Ben Athiwaratkun, Qiushi Sun, Mi Zhang, Ping Luo, Wenhu Chen, Ngai Wong
papers.evidence: 跨平台计算机使用智能体的实时基准与执行环境
papers.tldr: 现有基准多把 web、移动与桌面环境割裂开来，难以检验单一通用智能体能否跨操作系统执行长程任务。作者提出 OS-Omni：一个覆盖 Windows、Ubuntu、macOS、iOS、Android 与 Web 的实时跨平台基准与执行环境，提供可复现初始化、平台适配器、轨迹日志与终态评估器。v1 包含每个平台 48 个任务，以及 12 个将桌面与安卓手机配对的跨端流程。最强智能体 Claude Opus 5.5 平均成功率 68.5%，低于人类 77.3%，且 iOS 与 macOS 落后超过 25 分，说明平台鲁棒的长程计算机使用仍未解决。
papers.abstract_en: Computer-using agents are increasingly expected to complete realistic user goals rather than isolated GUI actions. However, existing benchmarks typically isolate web, mobile, or desktop environments, leaving it unclear whether a single generalist agent can execute long-horizon workflows that span multiple operating systems and persistent application states. We introduce OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment for evaluating computer-using agents across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. OS-Omni is released in versioned waves of 300 tasks each; this paper focuses on the first release, v1, which contains 48 tasks per platform and 12 cross-platform workflows that pair a desktop with an Android phone. OS-Omni provides reproducible initialization, platform-specific adapters, trajectory logging, and executable final-state evaluators, and includes controlled service-backed applications for workflows involving account, cart, budget, calendar, message, and other persistent state. Human studies show that OS-Omni tasks require 67.54 interaction steps, substantially exceeding OSWorld references of 15.0 steps. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, trailing the 77.3% human reference by 8.8 points; the gap is uneven across platforms, with frontier models exceeding humans on Linux but trailing them by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS. These results indicate that current agents remain far from platform-robust, long-horizon computer use, especially when success requires sustained state tracking and durable final-state changes.
